short: India has no AI act. The binding layer is the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and its 2025 Rules, phased in over 18 months, with penalties of up to Rs 250 crore, plus sector guidance such as the RBI's FREE-AI framework.
title: India AI Laws
subtitle: No AI act: the DPDP Act and sector regulators bind
body_html:
Status at a glance

No AI act; privacy and sector law bind. India has no standalone AI statute. The enforceable layer is the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, made operational by the DPDP Rules, 2025, which the government notified on 14 November 2025 with an eighteen-month period for phased compliance. Sector regulators add their own expectations: the Reserve Bank of India's FREE-AI Committee report of 13 August 2025 sets out what the RBI expects of the banks and lenders it regulates. The report is not binding, but supervisory expectations tend to become examination findings before they become law. Verified on 25 October 2026 against the Press Information Bureau and the RBI.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberPublishedIn force
Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023Act No. 22 of 20232023Operational with the Rules
Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025Notified 14 November 2025Phased over eighteen months
FREE-AI Committee Report: Framework for Responsible and Ethical Enablement of AIRBI report13 August 2025Not binding

Who regulates and enforces

  • Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY): makes the DPDP Rules and the IT Act rules.
  • Data Protection Board of India: enforces the DPDP Act; appeals go to the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal.
  • Reserve Bank of India: sets expectations for AI in regulated financial institutions.

Scope and reach

There is no AI-specific scope. The DPDP Act binds data fiduciaries that process digital personal data. Its territorial clause (section 3) was not re-read, because India Code answered this crawler 403, so its reach abroad is not stated here.

Core obligations

  • A separate, clear consent notice from every data fiduciary.
  • Reasonable security safeguards, and notice of a personal data breach to the Board and to the people affected.
  • Duties on processing children's data.
  • Consent managers must be companies incorporated in India.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Failure to keep reasonable security safeguardsRs 250 croreDPDP Act, Schedule, as the PIB fact sheet of November 2025 states itData Protection Board
Failure to notify a breach; breach of the duties on children's dataRs 200 crore eachDPDP Act, ScheduleData Protection Board
Any other breach of the Act or the RulesRs 50 croreDPDP Act, ScheduleData Protection Board

What is coming next

  • By May 2027: the end of the Rules' eighteen-month phase-in, counted from notification on 14 November 2025. The date each rule starts, including the consent-manager rule, is in the gazette notification, which was not readable from this crawler.

Sources

  • FREE-AI Committee Report, Reserve Bank of India

Last verified

25 October 2026, against the sources above. Not confirmed on an official source and therefore left out: the February 2026 IT Rules amendment on synthetically generated content and deepfake labelling, and the start date of each DPDP rule, because MeitY's pages, India Code and the e-Gazette could not be read from this crawler.
